A 57-key waterfront resort on 8.10 acres in Talbot County, Maryland.

Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island sits on Tilghman Island in Talbot County, Maryland, between the Chesapeake Bay and the Choptank River — an 8.10-acre waterfront parcel with 1,100 feet of water frontage, a marina, pool, restaurant and boat bar. Operated under the Wylder Hotels brand, the property is mid-repositioning, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2.

Ownership and operating structure.

The property is owned by 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC, led by principal John Flannigan, and operated under the Wylder Hotels brand through affiliate Wylder Eastern Shore Management, LLC — controlling day-to-day operations and the renovation, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2.

Ownership
21551 Tilghman Investors LLC
Principal
John Flannigan
Operator / Brand
Wylder Hotels
Manager
Wylder Eastern Shore Mgmt.
Structure and Alignment
01Owner-operated, no third-party manager — Day-to-day operations are run by an affiliate of ownership. There is no third-party management agreement to terminate or subordinate, no comfort letter to negotiate and no split incentive between owner and operator.
02Continuous ownership since 2017 — The sponsor has owned and operated the hotel under the Wylder brand through the pandemic cycle and the current repositioning, investing a further $642,693 of capital between 2021 and 2025.
03Single-asset ownership entity — 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC holds this property and no other operating assets, keeping the collateral and its cash flow ring-fenced.
04Two-property brand platform — Revenue management, distribution, design and procurement are shared across Wylder Hotels in Maryland and New York, giving a 57-key asset reach it could not support standing alone.

Operating statements are produced monthly at the property level and are the basis for the historical figures in this package. Financial reporting, revenue management and the renovation are handled in-house.

The Proof Case

Wylder Windham opened in 2022 after roughly $27,000,000 of investment and was named the number one resort in New York State the following year. The affiliation planned at Tilghman Island follows the same path, under the same ownership and the same management company.

Business plan and capital improvement program.

Capital Improvement Program $3.0M · $52,684 / key · Sep 2026 – Apr 2027
01
Guest room renovation
Full renovation of all 57 guest rooms at $25,000 per key. Four out-of-service keys are returned and three added in the back house, taking the hotel from 50 to 57 — 12.3% more sellable inventory that has never produced revenue.
$1.43M
02
Additional revenue sources
A marina expansion adding 25 slips, built for $250,000, carries almost no operating overhead and contributes roughly $146,000 a year at stabilization — payback inside two years on revenue never previously captured. A reconfigured boat bar and rebuilt three-bedroom house add further sources.
$0.85M
03
Brand affiliation
Operation under the Wylder Hotels brand, with a planned Small Luxury Hotels affiliation in Year 2 distributed through Hilton channels.
SLH · Yr 2

Exterior and interior improvements, contingency and professional fees complete the $3,003,000 program, equal to $52,684 per key across 57 keys. The program is funded by the sponsor outside this financing and is not drawn from loan proceeds.

The Model Room Is Built

The guest-room specification is complete and can be inspected on site. Finishes, casegoods, lighting, soft goods and bath are installed. The $25,000 per key in the budget is priced against a room that exists rather than a drawing, which takes design and specification risk out of the remaining keys and gives the schedule a known unit cost to roll out.

Small Luxury Hotels affiliation and distribution.

Why the Affiliation Matters
Hilton Distribution

SLH member hotels are bookable directly through Hilton.com, the Hilton app and Hilton Honors. The affiliation places the property inside Hilton’s reservation and loyalty system rather than leaving it dependent on direct booking and third-party channels, which is the mechanism behind the projected occupancy and rate gain.

An Established Relationship

The sponsor already operates within SLH. Wylder Windham, the sister hotel in the Catskills, is an SLH member and was the first in that market. The application here is an extension of a working relationship rather than a first approach.

American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts

Wylder Windham carries the American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts designation, reached through the SLH platform. The same designation is the plan at Tilghman Island, adding a high-rate corporate and affluent leisure channel on completion.

Affiliation is targeted on completion of the renovation and remains subject to application, inspection, board approval and an executed brand affiliate agreement.

Food and beverage cost of 60.0% against a 72.0% segment figure reflects a limited-menu seasonal outlet and event catering rather than a three-meal restaurant. The index fell between 2024 and 2025 because the property was discounting rate while carrying keys out of service — average rate dropped from $291 to $265 against a market holding $350. Rate, not occupancy, is the variance. Recovering it is what the capital program and the affiliation are for.

The market set totals 404 rooms including the subject and a composite of smaller properties. The subject holds 76% of market rate but only 58% of market occupancy, producing a RevPAR index of 44%. The business plan targets 70% of market RevPAR at stabilization — a level still 30% below the market average and below both luxury properties in the set. The STR benchmarking on the preceding page is drawn from a differently constituted set of four properties and 364 rooms; the two are not interchangeable.

What the Market Trend Supports

Market supply has been unchanged at approximately 404 rooms since 2022, while demand has grown in each of the last two years and reached a ten-year high of 84,017 room nights in 2025. Trailing twelve-month demand through March 2026 is running 5.6% ahead of the prior period. Market RevPAR has compounded at 6.0% a year since 2019 and stands at a record $199. The projections adopt none of this growth: rate and occupancy for the competitive market are held flat at 2025 levels throughout, so the entire RevPAR gain in the plan is attributed to the renovation, the seven added keys and the brand affiliation.

The Position

The as-is estimate of $368,421 per key sits below the average of both comparable sets — the East Coast waterfront sales and the eight resort trades closed since January 2025 — and between the median and the average of the more recent set.

The stabilized estimate of $500,000 per key sits below the two highest recent resort trades, at $741,000 and $893,000 per key, and is reached only after a $3,003,000 capital program and brand affiliation.

Total project cost basis of $327,713 per key remains below the as-is estimate, and the loan attaches at $221,053 per key.

The Tilghman Island Inn is the nearest transaction and is reported under contract at $5,200,000. It is a 20-key upper-midscale property configured as condominium units on five acres, with 1,800 SF of meeting space and seven slips. It carries neither the key count, the two food and beverage outlets, the marina, the 3,722 SF of event space nor the income base of the subject, and it establishes small-inn pricing on the island rather than resort pricing.

What the Local Set Does Establish

The Tidewater Inn, an 89-key full-service hotel in Easton, is expected to be brought to market in 2026 and reported 2025 occupancy of 48% at a $238 average rate on approximately $950,000 of net operating income. It is the only property in the local set operating at institutional scale, and it does so at a rate 43% below the subject’s $415 stabilized projection and without waterfront, marina or resort positioning. The Robert Morris Inn in Oxford, 16 keys, traded at $200,000 per key in 2024 and is now closed and back on the market at a lower asking price. The local evidence brackets the subject rather than pricing it: small and partly distressed inns below, and a single larger property in a materially different product tier.

The eight resort transactions at left average 44 keys, closely matching the subject at 57, and support a per-key range of $266,000 to $893,000 with a median of $332,000. The estimated as-is value of $368,421 per key sits between that median and the average.
